references.text: The continuation of the law regarding entrusted property, where the case is brought before God (האלהים) to determine guilt between the parties.
A parallel law concerning entrusted property in which an oath to the Lord is used to decide whether someone has wronged another's property.
The use of האלהים (God/judges) in a legal context, where the master must bring his servant before God.
Instructions on bringing difficult legal cases to priests and judges for judgment.
An oath sworn to the Lord as a method to determine guilt in cases where there are no witnesses.
Solomon's prayer that God would judge between the guilty and the innocent when someone swears an oath in the temple.
Confirms that an oath calls upon God as witness and ends all dispute among people.
Both verses illustrate the law's mechanism for handling unresolved questions of guilt where no human party can be identified, thus transferring the case to God's representative.
Both verses illustrate the law's mechanism for dealing with unexplained crimes where the perpetrator is unknown by involving the holy place.
